ECE 6612

Security goals and network layers

From the figure to the concept

Fig. 1 shows a browser request traveling from a local network through intermediaries to an application.

A browser sends an application request inside several envelopes. HTTP supplies the request meaning; TCP supplies a reliable byte stream; IP supplies addresses for routing; and the local link carries a frame to the next device. Each receiving layer processes its own header. Routers usually replace link headers at each hop while forwarding the IP packet toward its destination.

A threat model states what needs protection, who may attack it, what the attacker can observe or change, and which components remain trusted. A passive observer records traffic. An active intermediary can also delay, discard, modify or inject it. An off-path attacker usually has to guess hidden connection values to make an injected message acceptable. A compromised endpoint can access data after the network encryption terminates.

Confidentiality protects message contents from unauthorized readers. Integrity protects against unauthorized changes, and authentication associates a message or peer with a key or identity. Availability concerns whether legitimate users can obtain service. Freshness concerns whether a message belongs to the current exchange. These goals require separate checks: an authentic old request can still repeat an unwanted transaction.

The cryptographic algorithm can be public; the secret key supplies the protected knowledge. For a uniformly random k-bit key, exhaustive search has 2^k candidates and takes about 2^(k−1) trials on average. This average assumes an arbitrary order of distinct guesses and a way to recognize the right key. Password-derived keys inherit the password search space as well as the derivation cost.

Attacker access matters when interpreting a cryptographic claim. In a known-plaintext attack, some plaintext and matching ciphertext are available. Chosen-plaintext access lets an attacker request encryption of selected messages; chosen-ciphertext access lets an attacker submit selected ciphertexts to a decryption interface under the stated restrictions. Secure designs specify the attack model instead of relying on a hidden algorithm.

Layer boundaries identify where protection ends. Wi-Fi encryption protects the radio link to the access point. TLS can protect the application stream from the browser to the website even when intermediaries control routing. The path still reveals traffic timing, packet lengths and destination addressing to relevant observers. A useful analysis names the exact protected span and then follows what each actor receives.

Example

A document service sends a file through a café access point. A passive observer can measure when packets arrive. With correctly authenticated TLS and uncompromised endpoints, the file contents remain protected across that access point. If the observer discards every packet, the connection loses availability. These outcomes concern different goals and can occur during the same connection.

Practice

1. A router on the path can discard packets but cannot obtain the TLS traffic keys. Which security goal can it directly defeat, and which observations can it still make?

Trace both the delivery decision and the headers outside TLS.

It can defeat availability by dropping traffic. It can observe IP addressing, packet sizes and timing at its position. Correct TLS record protection preserves application confidentiality and integrity against that router under the stated key and endpoint assumptions.

2. A protocol accepts an old, correctly authenticated transfer request twice. Identify the missing check and describe one concrete state value that supplies it.

The second copy carries the same bytes and tag.

The receiver needs a freshness or replay check. It can authenticate a monotonically increasing transaction number and retain the largest accepted value, rejecting reused or older numbers according to the protocol. Reliable state handling across retries and restarts is part of this design.
